learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected About twice as big and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Mercator equator area ratio 1.00. At 30 N area 1.34, stretch 1.15 and width height 0.99. At 60 N area 4.16, stretch 2.00 and width height 0.98. Equal Earth at 60 N gave area 1.00 and width height 1.73. Home restored equator area 1.00 and shape ratio 0.74; restored 60 N.
observations.reveal: Corrected to about four times, explained two times stretch in each direction and finite-circle extra distortion, then equal-area shape change and unavoidable projection tradeoff.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected in both projections. Mercator northern circle was much larger and nearly round; Equal Earth northern oval and fixed equator oval had matching area. Reveal inner scroll clipped northern circle entirely at current position, though metrics and explanation were readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete area prediction tests confusing length with area.
prediction.evidence: Twice chosen against same and four times.

interaction.reason: Latitude and projection changes expose both area and shape tradeoffs.
interaction.evidence: 4.16 area at 60 N versus 1.00 after map switch.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains dimensional multiplication and acknowledges finite-circle difference.
payoff.evidence: Two times two gives four; top edge stretched more.

clarity.reason: Strong labels and ratios support contrast, but reveal clips the northern example from view.
clarity.evidence: Inner scroll at reveal left fixed circle only visible.

transfer.reason: General projection tradeoff supplied without a new use case.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard latitude reset worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Round shapes can carry fourfold area distortion.
surprise.evidence: Mercator 60 N area 4.16 with shape ratio 0.98.

visualExplanation.reason: Matched ground circles and two map types reveal an invisible representation tradeoff.
visualExplanation.evidence: Equal Earth area 1.00 with squashed oval versus Mercator enlarged circle.

playfulness.reason: Moving circles and switching maps invites comparison.

practicalValue.reason: Supports interpretation of world-map area claims.
practicalValue.evidence: Equal area versus shape preservation distinction.

depth.reason: Connects local scale, area multiplication and global map tradeoffs.
depth.evidence: Finite-circle qualification and sphere flattening limit.

complexity.reason: Direct visual comparison introduces geometry and representation tradeoffs.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish local shape, linear stretch and total area across map projections.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One slider, two presets and map toggle; inner scrolling at reveal.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Mercator and Equal Earth properties explained through controls.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Latitude, area and width-height multipliers plus two-dimensional multiplication.

whyCool: A map can keep a circle round while dramatically exaggerating its area.
caveat: Reveal layout hides the northern circle at the tested scroll position; both full map states were inspected before reveal.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
